name: Buck Converter Designer
blurb: inductor, output capacitor and ripple for a buck converter
intro: Sizes the power stage of a synchronous buck in continuous conduction: the inductor from the ripple current you allow at the highest input voltage, and the output capacitance for both the ripple and a load step. Formulas from TI SLVA477B plus the energy balance for load release.

inputs.label: Inductor ripple
inputs.help: Peak-to-peak ripple as a share of the output current; 20-40 % is the usual range.

inputs.label: Efficiency
inputs.help: Only corrects the duty cycle; take it from the controller's datasheet.

examples.title: 12 V to 3.3 V at 2 A, 500 kHz
5 V to 1.2 V at 3 A, 2 MHz

usage: Give input voltage min/max, output voltage (V), maximum output current (A), switching frequency (Hz, 500k accepted), ripple current as % of Iout, the output ripple in mV p-p, a load step in A with its allowed deviation in mV, efficiency in % and the controller's minimum on-time in ns. It returns the duty cycle range, the calculated and a standard inductance, ripple and peak/RMS inductor current (the saturation rating to buy), the minimum output capacitance and maximum ESR, and input capacitor RMS current. Use it to pick the inductor and capacitors before a detailed loop design.
sources: TI SLVA477B, Basic Calculation of a Buck Converter's Power Stage (eq. 1-13)
Load release: ½·L·(I1² − I2²) = ½·C·((Vout+ΔV)² − Vout²) (energy balance)
Loop-limited step: Cout ≥ ΔI / (2π·fc·ΔV) with fc = fsw/10 (rule of thumb)
